data.title: Pricing
data.tagline: Help visitors compare plans, cost, and included value
data.description: A pricing section should make plan differences, billing periods, limits, and extra fees understandable. Highlight a recommended option only when the reason is clear. Visitors need enough detail to choose without opening several hidden notes.

use: Show usage limits and included features
Lead to purchase or contact for a suitable plan
avoid: Hide required fees in fine print
Use plan names that reveal nothing about the difference
Mark a plan as recommended without a reason
Make visitors calculate the real price from scattered notes

lessonPractice.title: A subscription page offers Individual, Team, and Enterprise plans with monthly and annual billing. How can users compare real cost?

options.label: Compare intended users, core benefits, billing period, actual total, and cancellation terms
options.feedback: Together these determine fit and actual payment, allowing each plan to be compared on the same basis.

options.label: Emphasize only the lowest annual monthly equivalent and reveal the annual total at checkout
options.feedback: A monthly equivalent aids comparison, but hiding the charged total prevents users from judging real cost before selection.

options.label: Mark the highest-margin plan Most popular without an audience or evidence
options.feedback: Recommendations influence choice. Without evidence, the badge cannot show that the plan fits the current user.

data.agentPrompt: Audit the pricing section: state intended user, differentiating benefits, currency, billing period, charged total, renewal, and cancellation for every plan. Do not replace annual total with a monthly equivalent, remove unsupported popularity claims, and verify mobile comparison.
